# orders-service

HTTP API for customer accounts, orders, payments, and order exports.
Node.js 20 or later; no third-party dependencies.

```sh
npm test                                  # node --test
APP_SECRET=change-me REPORT_DIR=./reports \
ADMIN_EMAIL=ops@example.com ADMIN_PASSWORD=change-me-too npm start
```

## API

| Method | Path | Caller | Result |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| POST | `/users` | anyone | Register `{ email, password, name }`; 201 with the profile |
| POST | `/sessions` | anyone | `{ email, password }`; 201 with `{ token }` |
| GET | `/users/me` | customer | Own profile |
| GET | `/users` | admin | Page of profiles |
| POST | `/orders` | customer | `{ items: [{ sku, unitPrice, quantity }] }`; 201 with the order |
| GET | `/orders` | customer | Page of own orders; admins see every order |
| GET | `/orders/:id` | customer | One order |
| POST | `/orders/:id/cancel` | customer | Cancel an order |
| POST | `/orders/:id/ship` | admin | Mark a paid order shipped |
| POST | `/orders/:id/deliver` | admin | Mark a shipped order delivered |
| POST | `/payments` | customer | `{ orderId, amount }`; 201 with the payment, the order becomes `paid` |
| GET | `/payments/:id` | customer | One payment |
| POST | `/reports/orders` | admin | Export every order as CSV; 201 with `{ name }` |
| GET | `/reports/:name` | admin | Download an export |

## Rules

- Requests authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Tokens are
  signed with `APP_SECRET` and expire after one hour.
- Customers read and change only their own orders and payments. Admins read
  all of them.
- Order lifecycle: `pending` → `paid` → `shipped` → `delivered`. A customer
  may cancel an order while it is `pending` or `paid`; a shipped or delivered
  order can no longer be cancelled.
- `unitPrice`, `amount`, and `total` are numbers in the currency unit with at
  most two decimals. An order total is exact to the cent.
- A payment amount must equal the order total.
- List endpoints accept `page` (1-based, default 1) and `pageSize` (default
  20, maximum 100) and return `{ items, page, pageSize, total, totalPages }`.
  `totalPages` is the number of pages needed to show every item, at least 1.
- Exports are written to and served from `REPORT_DIR`.
- Errors return `{ error }` with 400 for invalid input, 401 when
  unauthenticated, 403 for a missing role, 404 for unknown resources and for
  resources the caller may not see, and 409 for a state conflict.

# orders-service

HTTP API for customer accounts, orders, payments, and order exports.
Node.js 20 or later; no third-party dependencies.

```sh
npm test                                  # node --test
APP_SECRET=change-me REPORT_DIR=./reports \
ADMIN_EMAIL=ops@example.com ADMIN_PASSWORD=change-me-too npm start
```

## API

| Method | Path | Caller | Result |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| POST | `/users` | anyone | Register `{ email, password, name }`; 201 with the profile |
| POST | `/sessions` | anyone | `{ email, password }`; 201 with `{ token }` |
| GET | `/users/me` | customer | Own profile |
| GET | `/users` | admin | Page of profiles |
| POST | `/orders` | customer | `{ items: [{ sku, unitPrice, quantity }] }`; 201 with the order |
| GET | `/orders` | customer | Page of own orders; admins see every order |
| GET | `/orders/:id` | customer | One order |
| POST | `/orders/:id/cancel` | customer | Cancel an order |
| POST | `/orders/:id/ship` | admin | Mark a paid order shipped |
| POST | `/orders/:id/deliver` | admin | Mark a shipped order delivered |
| POST | `/payments` | customer | `{ orderId, amount }`; 201 with the payment, the order becomes `paid` |
| GET | `/payments/:id` | customer | One payment |
| POST | `/reports/orders` | admin | Export every order as CSV; 201 with `{ name }` |
| GET | `/reports/:name` | admin | Download an export |

## Rules

- Requests authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Tokens are
  signed with `APP_SECRET` and expire after one hour.
- Customers read and change only their own orders and payments. Admins read
  all of them.
- Order lifecycle: `pending` → `paid` → `shipped` → `delivered`. A customer
  may cancel an order while it is `pending` or `paid`; a shipped or delivered
  order can no longer be cancelled.
- `unitPrice`, `amount`, and `total` are numbers in the currency unit with at
  most two decimals. An order total is exact to the cent.
- A payment amount must equal the order total.
- List endpoints accept `page` (1-based, default 1) and `pageSize` (default
  20, maximum 100) and return `{ items, page, pageSize, total, totalPages }`.
  `totalPages` is the number of pages needed to show every item, at least 1.
- Exports are written to and served from `REPORT_DIR`.
- Errors return `{ error }` with 400 for invalid input, 401 when
  unauthenticated, 403 for a missing role, 404 for unknown resources and for
  resources the caller may not see, and 409 for a state conflict.

Read-only audit of `src/` against `README.md`, then a fix for each defect that
reproduced. Six defects reproduced before the change and no longer reproduce
after it. The visible suite passed with all six present, so each fixed
behaviour gained a regression test.

## What changed

### Security

**1. Any customer could read any other customer's order** — `src/orders/routes.js`

`GET /orders/:id` called `orders.get(id)`, which does no ownership check, while
every sibling route used `orders.getOwned(user, id)`. Any authenticated
customer could read another customer's order — items, prices, total, and the
owner's user id — by guessing or obtaining its id. README: "Customers read and
change only their own orders and payments." Now uses `getOwned`, so a non-owner
gets 404, matching the README rule that an invisible resource is a 404.

**2. Report download could read any file on disk** — `src/reports/routes.js`

`GET /reports/:name` passed the path parameter straight into
`path.join(reportDir, params.name)`. The router URI-decodes path parameters, so
`GET /reports/..%2F..%2Fetc%2Fpasswd` escaped `REPORT_DIR` and returned the
file's contents to any admin. Export names are generated by this module, so the
fix is a whitelist on the generated shape (`/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.csv$/`): no path
separator, and no dot in the stem, so `..` cannot be formed. A rejected name
returns 404 rather than 400, because a name that cannot denote a report is
indistinguishable from a report that does not exist.

**3. Login response time revealed which emails are registered** — `src/users/service.js`

`verifyCredentials` returned early when no user matched, skipping the scrypt
hash. A registered email cost ~20 ms, an unknown one ~0.7 ms — a 28x difference,
measurable remotely, which turns the login endpoint into an account-enumeration
oracle. It now compares against a per-process dummy hash when no user matches,
so both paths perform exactly one scrypt and one `timingSafeEqual`.

### Correctness

**4. Order totals were not exact to the cent** — `src/lib/money.js`, `src/orders/service.js`

`sumLines` summed `unitPrice * quantity` in floating point, so an order for 3
items at 0.1 was stored and served with `total: 0.30000000000000004`. README:
"An order total is exact to the cent." Totals are now accumulated in integer
cents and converted once at the end.

**5. `totalPages` under-reported the number of pages** — `src/lib/pagination.js`

`Math.floor(items.length / pageSize)` instead of `Math.ceil`. With 24 orders at
`pageSize=10` the response said `totalPages: 2` while page 3 held 4 more items,
so a client paginating on `totalPages` silently dropped the last partial page.
Any item count below one page already reported 1 via the `Math.max(1, …)`
clamp, which is why no visible test caught it.

**6. Shipped orders could be cancelled** — `src/orders/service.js`

`TRANSITIONS.shipped` listed `cancelled`. README: "a shipped or delivered order
can no longer be cancelled." Removed; `shipped` now transitions only to
`delivered`.

### Dead code

- **`parseCookies`** (`src/http/respond.js`) — removed. No caller anywhere in
  `src/` or `test/`; the service authenticates by `Authorization` header only
  and reads no cookies.
- **`registerProvider`** (`src/payments/providers.js`) — removed. Exported but
  never called from outside the module, which called it once at load time to
  register the single `manual` provider. Its validation guarded a call site
  that does not exist. The provider table is now a module constant, and
  `getProvider` keeps the `provider: '<name>'` option and its unknown-name
  error unchanged. A `Map` rather than an object literal, so a name like
  `constructor` cannot resolve through the prototype chain.
- **`users.toPublic`** (`src/users/service.js`) — dropped from the service's
  public surface; it existed only for the route fixed below.

### Simplification

**Order total had two implementations.** `src/payments/service.js` carried its
own `orderTotalCents`, correctly summing in cents, while `src/orders/service.js`
summed in floats. The two disagreed for the same order: payment validation
accepted the exact total while the API advertised the inexact one, so defect 4
could not be observed through the payment path. Cent arithmetic now lives in
`src/lib/money.js` (`toCents`, `fromCents`, `totalCents`) and the payment
service compares the submitted amount against `order.total`. The orders
subsystem owns the total; payments reads it.

**The user route reached past its service into the store.** `GET /users` built
its response from `store.list('users').map(users.toPublic)` inside
`src/users/routes.js` — the only reason the route layer received `store` at all,
and the only list endpoint that paginated in the route rather than the service
(`orders.list` paginates in the service). Replaced with `users.list(query)`;
`store` is no longer passed to `registerUserRoutes`, so the route layer now
depends only on services.

All commands run from the repository root on Node.js 20+, Windows.

**Baseline before any change** — `node --test`:

```
ℹ tests 20
ℹ pass 20
ℹ fail 0
```

**After the change** — `node --test`:

```
ℹ tests 25
ℹ pass 25
ℹ fail 0
```

**The five new tests fail against the original source.** Restoring `src/` from
`HEAD` and running the new suite (`git checkout HEAD -- src && node --test`):

```
✖ an order is hidden from customers who do not own it
✖ an order total is exact to the cent
✖ a shipped or delivered order can no longer be cancelled
✖ a page reports every page needed to show its items
✖ a report name cannot reach outside the report directory

ℹ pass 20
ℹ fail 5
```

test used two line items (0.1x3 plus 0.2x1) whose float errors cancelled, so it
passed against the buggy code. It was rewritten around single line items
(0.1x3 -> 0.3, 1.1x3 -> 3.3), where the error is observable.

**End-to-end probe against a live server**, driving the real HTTP surface with
an admin and two customers, before and after. A file was planted next to
`REPORT_DIR` for the traversal probe:

| Probe | Before | After |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `GET /orders/:id` for another customer's order | `200` with the full order | `404 {"error":"order not found"}` |
| Order total for 0.1 x 3 | `0.30000000000000004` | `0.3` |
| `GET /orders?pageSize=10` over 24 orders | `totalPages: 2`, page 3 holds 4 items | `totalPages: 3` |

| `GET /reports/..%2FSECRET-OUTSIDE.txt` | `200` with the outside file's contents | `404 {"error":"report not found"}` |

0.1 x 3 -> 0.3
12.5x2 + 5x1 -> 30
24 items, pageSize 10 -> totalPages 3
0 items -> totalPages 1
2 items -> totalPages 1
```

`parseCookies`, `registerProvider`, and `users.toPublic` had no remaining
caller, and the post-change grep is clean.

- **The timing fix has no automated test.** A latency assertion is flaky under
  CI load, so the 20.1 ms / 20.1 ms result above is a one-off manual
  measurement on one machine, five samples per branch, median reported. It is
  not protected against regression.
- **Three defects I found and deliberately left alone**, because each is a
  design gap rather than a reproduced defect, and fixing them exceeds this
  audit's scope. Each needs its own decision:
  - `src/auth/tokens.js` compares the HMAC with `!==`, a non-constant-time
    string comparison. I did not attempt to measure, let alone exploit, it; a
    remote timing attack against a base64url digest comparison across an HTTP
    stack is not practically mountable, but the constant-time fix is cheap.
  - `src/http/respond.js` rejects a body over 1 MiB only at `end`, discarding
    the excess without destroying the socket. Memory stays bounded; a client
    can still make the server read an arbitrarily large upload.
  - `POST /sessions` has no rate limit or lockout, so passwords can be
    brute-forced at whatever rate scrypt allows (~20 ms per attempt).

  `src/store/memoryStore.js` holds everything in memory. The total now comes
  from `order.total` instead of being recomputed from the items; with a real
  datastore, orders written by the old code would carry inexact totals and the
  change would need a staged migration. `toCents` would round them to the
  intended value, but that was not tested against stored data, because there is

  read-modify-write without locking (`orders.markPaid` after
  `payments.capture`), which a single-threaded Node process serializes today;
  I did not analyse it for a multi-process deployment.
- **I did not run the server as documented in the README** (`npm start` with
  `APP_SECRET`/`REPORT_DIR`/`ADMIN_*`). Every probe used `createApp` over a
  real HTTP listener, which is what the test helper does.

```
src/app.js                |  2 +-
src/http/respond.js       | 12 +-----------
src/lib/money.js          | 18 ++++++++++++------
src/lib/pagination.js     |  2 +-
src/orders/routes.js      |  4 ++--
src/orders/service.js     |  6 +++---
src/payments/providers.js | 25 +++++++++----------------

src/users/service.js      | 22 ++++++++++++++++-----
test/orders.test.js       | 47 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
test/reports.test.js      | 14 ++++++++++++++
```

# Structural Simplification

>    globally only when the semantics, lifecycle, and constraints actually fit.

>    handling it when functionality, migration, rollback, and external
>    constraints permit removal.

---

## Reporting Vocabulary

The skill may reason with axis symbols, but reports are for a coding agent that
must choose an edit, test, lint rule, or rejection. Use the coder-facing field
names below in every emit block, gate table, and cross-skill citation.

| Internal symbol  | Coder-facing field used in reports                                    |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ΔD` (diversity) | **Subsystem-kinds Δ** — distinct subsystem/interface/pattern types added or removed |
| `ΔK` (coupling)  | **Dependency-edges Δ** — imports, calls, package edges, or runtime links added or removed |
| `ΔP` (depth)     | **Max-chain-depth Δ** — longest import/call/build chain before vs after |
| `Δn` (quantity)  | **Subsystem-count Δ** — files, subsystems, jobs, services, or instances added or removed |

| Axis          | Symbol | What it counts                      | Measurement recipe                                                    |
| ------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| **Coupling**  | `K`    | Relationship count and density      | Count edges, then compute density (`edges / (n × (n−1))` for directed graphs where `n > 1`) after defining edge kind and direction |
| **Depth**     | `P`    | Longest chain from source to sink   | Longest path from any origin to any terminus in the DAG               |
| **Quantity**  | `n`    | Total number of subsystems          | Direct count of subsystems (use §2 to identify them in your domain)   |

Domain-agnostic. *Subsystem* = any discrete node of the structure under
review — §2 names it per domain (a function, a service, a screen, a role, a
step); *relationships* = any connection (dependency, flow, sequence,
authority). Multi-axis interactions

domain's actual constraints.

> breaks the DAG assumption only when the chosen projection is required to be
> acyclic, such as imports, ownership, authority, or layer dependencies. See §5
> for the topology framing that rules those cycles out;

> enforceable static constraints to `architecture-as-code`. If the domain
> intentionally contains cycles

> cycle semantics before scoring.

---

## 2. Domain Mapping

| Domain                | Subsystems (nodes)                                  | Relationships (edges)                                                       |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Code                  | Subsystems, functions                               | Dependencies, calls, imports                                                |
| Project organization  | Repos, packages, workspaces, build targets          | Package dependencies, version constraints, build-time references, ownership |
| Runtime / deployment  | Services, processes, containers, instances, threads | RPC/HTTP calls, message flows, network paths, replication, lifecycle order  |
| Data model            | Entities, fields, types                             | References, joins, constraints                                              |
| Workflow              | Steps, stages, decisions                            | Transitions, triggers, sequencing                                           |
| UI / spatial          | Screens, regions, elements                          | Navigation, data flow, visual links                                         |
| Organization (people) | Roles, teams, systems                               | Authority, communication, data exchange                                     |
| Temporal              | Events, states, phases                              | Causal or sequential ordering                                               |

---

## 3. Heuristic Checks

Fast proxies — not substitutes for measurement.

| Check            | Signal                                                  | Axis          |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| **Symmetry**     | Structure more uniform after                            | D↓            |
| **Vocabulary**   | Describable with fewer concepts                         | D↓            |
| **Boundary**     | Fewer relationships crossing boundaries                 | K↓            |

---

Each axis has its own operation family — D↓ reduce diversity, K↓ reduce
coupling, P↓ reduce depth, n↓ reduce quantity — plus multi-axis moves, each
with guardrails on what it may claim. Read
[references/reduction-operations.md](references/reduction-operations.md)
when proposing a simpler alternative, a SIMPLIFY, or a redesign, or when
§6 cites a §4 warning; a measurement of a given candidate's four deltas does
not need it.

## 5. Topology Constraint

Treat a dependency structure as a directed topology with explicit positions,
interfaces, locality, and separately measured relationship fields. Bounded
public surfaces and local neighbor sets cap K, directional static edges cap P,
cohesive positions bound n, and consistent subsystem forms cap D. Decompose
along domain, abstraction-tier, or layer seams only when the proposed cut
improves the measured vector. Decomposition splits one subsystem into several;
aspect extraction pulls one aspect out of several subsystems. They are
different cuts; judge both by the vector.

scoring trade-offs. For runtime feedback, name the cycle semantics and measure
the chosen acyclic projection separately.

enforcement handoffs, see `morphogenetic-architecture`.

---

Reducing one axis usually raises another. Examples lean software but the
moves apply to any structure.

| Merge two cohesive subsystems                       | ↓   | within ↑ | ↓       | ↓   | Candidate proceed; verify internal K stays bounded            |
| Split overloaded subsystem along an SoC seam        | ↓   | ↓        | ↑       | ↑   | Candidate proceed; verify caller paths remain understandable  |

---

Cases where net axis effect is positive despite local cost.

### 7a. Conformance (Pattern Alignment)

Accept local structural cost to eliminate a unique shape from D only when the
standard pattern fits the same semantics, lifecycle, ownership, and external
constraints. One snowflake among ten uniform subsystems can inflate D
disproportionately, but a real domain distinction should be named and preserved.

### 7b. Scope Reduction (Deletion)

Remove or deprecate special functionality if its structural footprint exceeds
its utility and the `functionality-complexity-tradeoff` verdict allows safe
removal. Special cases are complexity multipliers: D↑ (unique patterns), K↑
(conditional paths), P↑ (extended chains), n↑ (supporting subsystems). The cost of
a feature includes every special case it forces elsewhere, plus the migration
and compatibility work needed to remove it safely.

### 7c. Atomicity Requirements

When an action coordinates multiple independent participants (services,
actors, steps, partners), the atomicity decision has direct structural cost.
Decide **before implementation** — see `architecture-guidelines` §5
*Atomicity*.

| Decision             | Structural effect | Action                                        |
| -------------------- | ----------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| Atomicity required   | K↑ P↑             | Accept coupling; use fail-fast / compensation |
| Eventual consistency | K↓ P↓             | Document acceptable partial-failure states    |

**Anti-Pattern:** designing multi-step operations without deciding atomicity
first.

---

## 8. Decision Protocol

1. **Model** before-state and after-state. Record D, K, P, n for each
   (internal axes; see Reporting Vocabulary for the coder-facing field names).
2. **Cycle check.** If the modeled projection is required to be acyclic, a
   cycle in the after-state is a hard fault — fix before continuing. If the
   domain permits cycles, record the cycle semantics and score the chosen
   acyclic projection separately.
3. **Answer the forcing questions in writing** (one line each):
    - **D:** What unique pattern does this introduce that no sibling uses?
      *(Name the 2nd concrete instance; absence = Rule-of-3 violation.)*
    - **K:** Which previously-independent subsystems does this link?
    - **P:** How long is the longest dependency chain a typical change
      traverses? *(>3 hops → max-chain-depth is itself the cost.)*
    - **n:** If deleted, what would dependents do? *(If "use the thing it
      wraps," it's a no-op facade.)*
    - **Counterfactual:** Does §7a or §7b apply? What is the 12-month
      removal cost?
4. **Check non-structural gates.** Confirm the candidate still satisfies
   required behavior, security/privacy, compliance, observability,
   performance, migration, and rollback constraints. Structural improvement is
   not permission to break a required property.
5. **Classify**:

    | Pattern                           | Action                          |
    | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
    | All axes improve or hold          | Proceed if non-structural gates pass |
    | Mixed (some improve, some worsen) | Consult §6 trade-offs, apply §7, then check gates |
    | No axis improves                  | Reject or redesign unless required by an external gate |

6. **Emit a coder-facing decision record** (see Reporting Vocabulary for the symbol mapping):

    ```
    Subject:              <structure / subsystem / refactor under review>
    Decision:             Proceed | Redesign | Reject

    Subsystem-kinds Δ:    <±n>   (evidence: novel pattern, 2nd concrete instance)
    Dependency-edges Δ:   <±n>   (evidence: what newly couples to what)
    Max-chain-depth Δ:    <±n>   (evidence: longest path before → after)
    Subsystem-count Δ:    <±n>   (evidence: subsystems added / removed)
    Cycle:                Pass | Fail
    Non-structural gates: Pass | Fail | Not evaluated
    Trade-off:            <§6 row matched; §7 sub-section if asymmetric>
    Rationale:            <1–3 sentences tying the four deltas and forcing-Q answers → decision>
    Next action:          <edit, test, lint rule, measurement, or smaller alternative>
    Verification:         <command / graph check / review evidence, or Not run + reason>
    ```

> [!IMPORTANT] If no axis improves, state: *"Complexity Warning:
> Subsystem-kinds Δ [X], Dependency-edges Δ [Y], Max-chain-depth Δ [Z],
> Subsystem-count Δ [W]. A simpler alternative is [...]."*

addresses occur in this context?), then a **worth ledger** (does the value

>    impossible state has no product value for that failure mode: skip the

>    executable invariant (§1c).

>    independently; never collapse into a single number.

>    failed necessity gate prefers safe removal or deprecation to elaborate

>    compatibility constraints.

>    linked outcome evidence when available. Completion, deployment, or adoption

>    dictates a worth decision. `requirements-grounding` owns the hypothesis's

Four interrogations — necessity, value, cost, counterfactual — each exposing a
common failure mode. Read
[references/forcing-questions.md](references/forcing-questions.md) before any
value scoring.

---

## 6. Decision Protocol

1. **Frame the subject.** Prospective: state it in one sentence, _"This
   allows [who] to [do what] so that [outcome]."_ Retrospective: define the
   boundary — files, symbols, entry points, feature flags, routes, or callers.
2. **Run the necessity gate** (§1); in retrospective mode walk the §1b
   heuristics before any worth scoring. On failure, emit per §1 and skip the
   remaining steps. A prospective necessity failure is rare but
   consequential: it stops a build that would have produced dead code on day
   one.
3. **Score `V` axes** (`U, F, R, I`) on a 0–3 scale with one-line evidence
   per axis.
    - Prospective evidence: user interviews, request tickets, analytics of the
      workaround, competitor behavior. Opinions are not evidence and cannot
      support a high-confidence build decision. Linked outcome hypotheses
      before release express expected value, not observed impact.
    - Retrospective evidence is usage data: telemetry hits per time window and
      user cohort; reach as the unique users or flows that enter the path;
      irreplaceability as whether an alternative path exists and users
      already use it. **If `V` cannot be measured, that itself is a finding**
      — instrument, identify an external floor (§8c), or keep confidence Low.
    - Consume current outcome-evidence records from
      `requirements-traceability`: cite the hypothesis ID, state, freshness,
      and observation identity, and preserve the canonical hypothesis
      version, cohort, threshold, window, and guardrails; never replace them
      with a more favorable interpretation. `stale` or `inconclusive`
      evidence cannot support High value confidence; `rejected` evidence
      lowers the supported value claim but does not by itself prove zero
      value.
4. **Score `C` axes**:
    - Delegate `D, K, P, n` to `structural-simplification`: deltas against a
      **concrete implementation sketch** (files touched, new abstractions or
      dependencies introduced, tests required, failure modes created) in
      prospective mode; absolute measured values in retrospective mode.
    - Score `Maintenance, Risk, Evolution` on 0–3 with one-line evidence per
      axis. Retrospective sources: `Maintenance` from dedicated tests, doc
      pages, recent commit churn, and dependency drift; `Risk` from bug ticket
      history, incident postmortems, and security or performance hotspot
      reports; `Evolution` from the count of PRs or design docs where the
      feature caused scope expansion, workarounds, or delays.
5. **Record confidence** (Low / Medium / High) for each side independently.
6. **Compare across both ledgers** without summing.
7. **Classify** using the Worth Matrix (§6a) and apply the confidence gate
   (§6b).
8. **Emit** the Output Contract (§9).

> [!NOTE] A retrospective audit with no telemetry available should first
> return an instrumentation task, not a verdict — **unless** the necessity
> gate has already produced a finding: you cannot measure usage of a code
> path that cannot be triggered. Deleting a feature merely because you cannot
> see it being used is survivorship bias in reverse; removing it because the
> failure mode it guards against cannot occur is structural reasoning.

### 6a. The Worth Matrix

|              | **Low C**            | **Medium C**             | **High C**       |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **High V**   | BUILD / KEEP         | BUILD / KEEP             | NEGOTIATE (§8)   |
| **Medium V** | BUILD-minimal / KEEP | BUILD-minimal / SIMPLIFY | DEFER / SIMPLIFY |
| **Low V**    | DEFER / QUARANTINE   | DROP / SIMPLIFY          | DROP / DELETE    |

retrospective (keep / simplify / delete). Necessity failures bypass the matrix.

### 6b. Confidence gate

A verdict carries the confidence of its weakest input. If either `V` or `C`
confidence is **Low**:

- **Prospective** → default to DEFER. Gather evidence before committing to
  high-cost action.
- **Retrospective** → default to QUARANTINE (§7b) and revisit with measured
  data for the low side.

Do not commit to irreversible verdicts (BUILD, DELETE) on low-confidence
estimates. **OBSOLETE is exempt from the confidence gate** when the
necessity finding is itself High confidence — a structural impossibility
does not become more or less impossible with more data.

may raise confidence only within the measured cohort, window, and guardrails.

outcome hypothesis.

|:--|:--|

| **NEGOTIATE** | High `V`, high `C`. Reduce scope, conform to an existing pattern (§7a of `structural-simplification`), or accept debt with an expiry date. |
| **DEFER** | `V` is unclear or evidence is thin. Document trigger conditions; revisit. |
| **DROP** | Does not clear the cost bar, OR fails the necessity gate (rationale: "guards against a state that cannot occur in this stack"). Record the rejection so the idea is not re-proposed without new evidence — or, for necessity failures, without a change in the stack's invariants. |

### 7b. Retrospective verdicts

| Verdict | Meaning |
|:--|:--|

> value evidence before KEEP. If it reduces to "it's defensive — just in case,"

    - Score `Maintenance, Risk, Evolution` on 0–3 with one-line evidence per
      axis. Retrospective sources: `Maintenance` from dedicated tests, doc
      pages, recent commit churn, and dependency drift; `Risk` from bug ticket
      history, incident postmortems, and security or performance hotspot
      reports; `Evolution` from the count of PRs or design docs where the
      feature caused scope expansion, workarounds, or delays.
5. **Record confidence** (Low / Medium / High) for each side independently.
6. **Compare across both ledgers** without summing.
7. **Classify** using the Worth Matrix (§6a) and apply the confidence gate
   (§6b).
8. **Emit** the Output Contract (§9).

> [!NOTE] A retrospective audit with no telemetry available should first
> return an instrumentation task, not a verdict — **unless** the necessity
> gate has already produced a finding: you cannot measure usage of a code
> path that cannot be triggered. Deleting a feature merely because you cannot
> see it being used is survivorship bias in reverse; removing it because the
> failure mode it guards against cannot occur is structural reasoning.

### 6a. The Worth Matrix

|              | **Low C**            | **Medium C**             | **High C**       |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **High V**   | BUILD / KEEP         | BUILD / KEEP             | NEGOTIATE (§8)   |
| **Medium V** | BUILD-minimal / KEEP | BUILD-minimal / SIMPLIFY | DEFER / SIMPLIFY |
| **Low V**    | DEFER / QUARANTINE   | DROP / SIMPLIFY          | DROP / DELETE    |

The first verdict in a cell is prospective (accept / reject), the second
retrospective (keep / simplify / delete). Necessity failures bypass the matrix.

### 6b. Confidence gate

A verdict carries the confidence of its weakest input. If either `V` or `C`
confidence is **Low**:

- **Prospective** → default to DEFER. Gather evidence before committing to
  high-cost action.
- **Retrospective** → default to QUARANTINE (§7b) and revisit with measured
  data for the low side.

Do not commit to irreversible verdicts (BUILD, DELETE) on low-confidence
estimates. **OBSOLETE is exempt from the confidence gate** when the
necessity finding is itself High confidence — a structural impossibility
does not become more or less impossible with more data.

An `unmeasured`, `inconclusive`, or `stale` outcome assessment keeps the affected
value claim Low unless independent current evidence supports it. `supported`
may raise confidence only within the measured cohort, window, and guardrails.
Authoritative floors in §8c remain source-driven and do not require an empirical
outcome hypothesis.

---

## 7. Verdicts

### 7a. Prospective verdicts

| Verdict | Meaning |
|:--|:--|
| **BUILD** | Proceed as specified. Record the worth rationale; it becomes the audit baseline. |
| **BUILD-minimal** | Build the smallest increment capturing ≥80% of `V`; defer the rest with explicit revisit triggers. |
| **NEGOTIATE** | High `V`, high `C`. Reduce scope, conform to an existing pattern (§7a of `structural-simplification`), or accept debt with an expiry date. |
| **DEFER** | `V` is unclear or evidence is thin. Document trigger conditions; revisit. |
| **DROP** | Does not clear the cost bar, OR fails the necessity gate (rationale: "guards against a state that cannot occur in this stack"). Record the rejection so the idea is not re-proposed without new evidence — or, for necessity failures, without a change in the stack's invariants. |

### 7b. Retrospective verdicts

| Verdict | Meaning |
|:--|:--|
| **KEEP** | Worth is positive. Document why — the rationale prevents a future audit from deleting it blindly. |
| **SIMPLIFY** | Worth is positive but `C` is inflated. Apply operations from `structural-simplification` §4. Re-score after. |
| **QUARANTINE** | `V` is unmeasured. Add telemetry; revisit after N weeks. |
| **DEPRECATE** | Marginal or negative worth; removal is non-trivial. Announce, migrate callers, remove on schedule. |
| **DELETE** | Negative worth, removal is feasible. Prefer removal over patching, but migrate callers, preserve compatibility promises, and keep rollback possible. |
| **OBSOLETE** | Necessity gate (§1) fails. Remove or deprecate the code without scoring worth; the rationale is structural (§1d). An invariant record nothing else captures is **SIMPLIFY** instead (§1c). |

> [!WARNING] "Interesting", "clever", and "elegant" are not verdicts.
> Cleverness imposes cost but rarely contributes measurable value. If a
> reviewer's rationale reduces to "it's nice that we have this," require
> value evidence before KEEP. If it reduces to "it's defensive — just in case,"
> apply the necessity gate before defaulting to KEEP.

---

# Audit and fix: orders-service

Read-only audit of `src/` against `README.md`, then a fix for each defect that
reproduced. Six defects reproduced before the change and no longer reproduce
after it. The visible suite passed with all six present, so each fixed
behaviour gained a regression test.

## What changed

### Security

**1. Any customer could read any other customer's order** — `src/orders/routes.js`

`GET /orders/:id` called `orders.get(id)`, which does no ownership check, while
every sibling route used `orders.getOwned(user, id)`. Any authenticated
customer could read another customer's order — items, prices, total, and the
owner's user id — by guessing or obtaining its id. README: "Customers read and
change only their own orders and payments." Now uses `getOwned`, so a non-owner
gets 404, matching the README rule that an invisible resource is a 404.

**2. Report download could read any file on disk** — `src/reports/routes.js`

`GET /reports/:name` passed the path parameter straight into
`path.join(reportDir, params.name)`. The router URI-decodes path parameters, so
`GET /reports/..%2F..%2Fetc%2Fpasswd` escaped `REPORT_DIR` and returned the
file's contents to any admin. Export names are generated by this module, so the
fix is a whitelist on the generated shape (`/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.csv$/`): no path
separator, and no dot in the stem, so `..` cannot be formed. A rejected name
returns 404 rather than 400, because a name that cannot denote a report is
indistinguishable from a report that does not exist.

**3. Login response time revealed which emails are registered** — `src/users/service.js`

`verifyCredentials` returned early when no user matched, skipping the scrypt
hash. A registered email cost ~20 ms, an unknown one ~0.7 ms — a 28x difference,
measurable remotely, which turns the login endpoint into an account-enumeration
oracle. It now compares against a per-process dummy hash when no user matches,
so both paths perform exactly one scrypt and one `timingSafeEqual`.

### Correctness

**4. Order totals were not exact to the cent** — `src/lib/money.js`, `src/orders/service.js`

`sumLines` summed `unitPrice * quantity` in floating point, so an order for 3
items at 0.1 was stored and served with `total: 0.30000000000000004`. README:
"An order total is exact to the cent." Totals are now accumulated in integer
cents and converted once at the end.

**5. `totalPages` under-reported the number of pages** — `src/lib/pagination.js`

`Math.floor(items.length / pageSize)` instead of `Math.ceil`. With 24 orders at
`pageSize=10` the response said `totalPages: 2` while page 3 held 4 more items,
so a client paginating on `totalPages` silently dropped the last partial page.
Any item count below one page already reported 1 via the `Math.max(1, …)`
clamp, which is why no visible test caught it.

**6. Shipped orders could be cancelled** — `src/orders/service.js`

`TRANSITIONS.shipped` listed `cancelled`. README: "a shipped or delivered order
can no longer be cancelled." Removed; `shipped` now transitions only to
`delivered`.

### Dead code

- **`parseCookies`** (`src/http/respond.js`) — removed. No caller anywhere in
  `src/` or `test/`; the service authenticates by `Authorization` header only
  and reads no cookies.
- **`registerProvider`** (`src/payments/providers.js`) — removed. Exported but
  never called from outside the module, which called it once at load time to
  register the single `manual` provider. Its validation guarded a call site
  that does not exist. The provider table is now a module constant, and
  `getProvider` keeps the `provider: '<name>'` option and its unknown-name
  error unchanged. A `Map` rather than an object literal, so a name like
  `constructor` cannot resolve through the prototype chain.
- **`users.toPublic`** (`src/users/service.js`) — dropped from the service's
  public surface; it existed only for the route fixed below.

### Simplification

**Order total had two implementations.** `src/payments/service.js` carried its
own `orderTotalCents`, correctly summing in cents, while `src/orders/service.js`
summed in floats. The two disagreed for the same order: payment validation
accepted the exact total while the API advertised the inexact one, so defect 4
could not be observed through the payment path. Cent arithmetic now lives in
`src/lib/money.js` (`toCents`, `fromCents`, `totalCents`) and the payment
service compares the submitted amount against `order.total`. The orders
subsystem owns the total; payments reads it.

**The user route reached past its service into the store.** `GET /users` built
its response from `store.list('users').map(users.toPublic)` inside
`src/users/routes.js` — the only reason the route layer received `store` at all,
and the only list endpoint that paginated in the route rather than the service
(`orders.list` paginates in the service). Replaced with `users.list(query)`;
`store` is no longer passed to `registerUserRoutes`, so the route layer now
depends only on services.

## Evidence

All commands run from the repository root on Node.js 20+, Windows.

**Baseline before any change** — `node --test`:

```
ℹ tests 20
ℹ pass 20
ℹ fail 0
```

**After the change** — `node --test`:

```
ℹ tests 25
ℹ pass 25
ℹ fail 0
```

**The five new tests fail against the original source.** Restoring `src/` from
`HEAD` and running the new suite (`git checkout HEAD -- src && node --test`):

```
✖ an order is hidden from customers who do not own it
✖ an order total is exact to the cent
✖ a shipped or delivered order can no longer be cancelled
✖ a page reports every page needed to show its items
✖ a report name cannot reach outside the report directory
ℹ tests 25
ℹ pass 20
ℹ fail 5
```

This check caught a hollow assertion: the first version of the cent-exactness
test used two line items (0.1x3 plus 0.2x1) whose float errors cancelled, so it
passed against the buggy code. It was rewritten around single line items
(0.1x3 to 0.3, 1.1x3 to 3.3), where the error is observable.

**End-to-end probe against a live server**, driving the real HTTP surface with
an admin and two customers, before and after. A file was planted next to
`REPORT_DIR` for the traversal probe:

| Probe | Before | After |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `GET /orders/:id` for another customer's order | `200` with the full order | `404 {"error":"order not found"}` |
| Order total for 0.1 x 3 | `0.30000000000000004` | `0.3` |
| `GET /orders?pageSize=10` over 24 orders | `totalPages: 2`, page 3 holds 4 items | `totalPages: 3` |
| `POST /orders/:id/cancel` on a shipped order | `200`, status `cancelled` | `409` |
| `GET /reports/..%2FSECRET-OUTSIDE.txt` | `200` with the outside file's contents | `404 {"error":"report not found"}` |
| `POST /sessions` latency, wrong password | known email 20.1 ms vs unknown 0.7 ms | 20.1 ms vs 20.1 ms |

**Unit-level checks** of the rewritten libraries (`node -e`):

```
0.1 x 3 -> 0.3
12.5x2 + 5x1 -> 30
24 items, pageSize 10 -> totalPages 3
0 items -> totalPages 1
2 items -> totalPages 1
```

**Dead-code claims** were established by `grep -rn` over `src/` and `test/`:
`parseCookies`, `registerProvider`, and `users.toPublic` had no remaining
caller, and the post-change grep is clean.

## What I did not verify

- **The timing fix has no automated test.** A latency assertion is flaky under
  CI load, so the 20.1 ms / 20.1 ms result above is a one-off manual
  measurement on one machine, five samples per branch, median reported. It is
  not protected against regression.
- **Three defects I found and deliberately left alone**, because each is a
  design gap rather than a reproduced defect, and fixing them exceeds this
  audit's scope. Each needs its own decision:
  - `src/auth/tokens.js` compares the HMAC with `!==`, a non-constant-time
    string comparison. I did not attempt to measure, let alone exploit, it; a
    remote timing attack against a base64url digest comparison across an HTTP
    stack is not practically mountable, but the constant-time fix is cheap.
  - `src/http/respond.js` rejects a body over 1 MiB only at `end`, discarding
    the excess without destroying the socket. Memory stays bounded; a client
    can still make the server read an arbitrarily large upload.
  - `POST /sessions` has no rate limit or lockout, so passwords can be
    brute-forced at whatever rate scrypt allows (~20 ms per attempt).
- **No persistence or rollout concern was assessed**, because
  `src/store/memoryStore.js` holds everything in memory. The total now comes
  from `order.total` instead of being recomputed from the items; with a real
  datastore, orders written by the old code would carry inexact totals and the
  change would need a staged migration. `toCents` would round them to the
  intended value, but that was not tested against stored data, because there is
  none.
- **No linter, type checker, or security scanner was run** — the project has
  none configured and declares no dependencies. `npm test` is the only gate.
  There is no CI workflow in the repository, so nothing enforces the new tests
  on a future change.
- **No load, concurrency, or crash-recovery testing.** The store performs
  read-modify-write without locking (`orders.markPaid` after
  `payments.capture`), which a single-threaded Node process serializes today;
  I did not analyse it for a multi-process deployment.
- **I did not run the server as documented in the README** (`npm start` with
  `APP_SECRET`/`REPORT_DIR`/`ADMIN_*`). Every probe used `createApp` over a
  real HTTP listener, which is what the test helper does.
